chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Returning to Cafe Society with Peter O'Brien
summary: Barney Josephson put in a piano; the union scale cost her thousands; young people came after the rock clubs closed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But in any event the first thing you did with him was when he told you to come to California?
No, he came from California and he dropped everything. He was going to school out there. I said if you go out with me and he said, "I'll come back." So that's what he did. He came back here.
And did you go to California then?

I didn't go to California with him, no. We've been out two years - that's been two years ago. He came back (?) we went down to Barney Josephson, the old night club owner of Cafe Society Uptown and Downtown. So he said he was down there feeling him out and couldn't get to him. He said, "Come on down town and talk to him." I said, "You're the one that's supposed to get the job, not me. I'm supposed to play after you get it." (LAUGHTER) I decided to go downtown with him. I was talking to Barney and I said, "Barney, put a piano over there," just like that. He said, "Oh, I have some customers here." He had some old customers that sat all day and read the paper and he said if they would hear music it would be terrible. I said, "Barney, put a piano over there." He thought about it and he said, "Go to the union and find out what kind of scale you can get." So I went to the union and I got a bigger scale for sidemen than I did for myself. That thing cost me about 3 or 4 thousand dollars. I had to save my

money for 4 weeks to pay my rent, electric light, and everything and I sat down there and played and Peter run around. For one thing all the rock places - you know that big place down there where Miles played - the Fillmore East - all the rock places closed and the kids used to come in and they were saying to their parents that they had found a new pianist and a new music. When someone came to the Cafe to tell me about it we just laughed like mad. A lot of times during that period they had a line. The kids they talked, talked, talked and when I got ready to leave, my land, they came to me and said, "Miss Williams, you're gonna really leave? Your music is so peaceful." I said, "I didn't think you were listening." So that was the beginning of our thing and we went through/and he borrowed a lot of strain money and he did a lot of things, from his parents and what-not. He's a real good friend to have.
This was what - 2 or 3 years ago?
